clue.text: Having used Monica, resorted to lying

indicators.note: read as re-sorted, these letters are sorted again into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who exploited a woman called Monica then fell back on telling lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resorted' reads as 'turned to', but split it as re-sorted and it sorts the letters of the two preceding words again.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendacious describes a person given to untruthfulness, so it is a direct adjective synonym for dishonest speech.

clue.text: A volume to absorb half-bookish type

indicators.note: something that absorbs takes another thing inside itself, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: taken as written
cc, cubic centimetres, is a measure of volume
demi- is the prefix for half, read here with an article in front

explanation.surface: A book seems to soak up half of a studious person.
explanation.walkthrough: A, then CC with A DEMI inside. The clue only prints one A, so the second one must come from reading 'half' as 'a half', a loose touch by the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: An academic is a scholar or university teacher, someone devoted to books and study, so the noun matches a scholarly person.

clue.text: This uniform is distinctive and reddish brown

blocks.note: first meaning: a distinctive uniform or colour scheme worn by servants or used by a company
second meaning: like liver in colour, an old adjective

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the rarer adjective formed from liver, describing the dark red-brown colour of that organ.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's uniform or colour design is called its livery, and the adjective liver-coloured describes a deep reddish-brown shade.

clue.text: Produce offspring, but no son initially for pop

indicators.note: but no means without, so the named letter is taken away
initially says the removal happens at the very front of the word

blocks.note: fish and frogs spawn when they produce young
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Having children, with no son at first, as a matter of father's choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like a dad, but it is British slang for pawning: to pop your watch is to hock it.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal British usage, to pop an item means to leave it with a pawnbroker as security for a loan.

clue.text: Fabric made completely out of rags?

blocks.note: tatters are rags, torn scraps of cloth
all means completely, as in all gone

explanation.surface: A cloth woven entirely from scraps, with a question mark for the whimsy.
explanation.walkthrough: Tattersall is a check pattern fabric named after the London horse market, and splits as 'tatters all'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattersall is a woollen cloth with a regular check pattern of coloured lines, often used for shirts.

clue.text: Would-be creating a name during a short burst of effort

indicators.note: something happening during another event sits inside its span, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: spirt is an old variant spelling of spurt, a brief burst of energy
a as written, plus N for name

explanation.surface: A hopeful whose reputation is forged in one quick dash of hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: SPIRT is a variant of spurt that crosswords use; AN sits inside A SPIRT.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirant is someone hoping to attain a position, so it serves as a noun for a would-be, a hopeful candidate.

clue.text: Puff about key to English novelist

indicators.note: the key to a word is what opens it, its opening letter
about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: to puff up is to swell
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Smoke or hype surrounding the essential element of an English writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Anna Sewell wrote Black Beauty. E goes inside SWELL after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna Sewell was a nineteenth-century English author whose only book, Black Beauty, became a classic horse story.

clue.text: Round pegs?

blocks.note: surface reading: pegs that are circular, as in square pegs in round holes
setter's reading: the small pegs a golfer uses during a round of golf

explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like a shape but is a noun: a golf round, where each hole starts with the ball on a small peg.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers place the ball on small wooden or plastic stands to drive off at each hole of the course.

clue.text: Girl has tot after consuming a Mexican dish

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it, so this piece goes round the next
consuming means swallowing, so the small word ends up inside the other

blocks.note: Ena is a girl's name
a tot is a small child
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl's toddler has eaten something, and the meal turns out Mexican.
explanation.walkthrough: Ena is an old-fashioned girl's name crosswords lean on; 'after consuming' means the tot has already eaten the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a Mexican tortilla rolled round a filling and baked under chilli sauce.

clue.text: Leather made to swing on being delivered

indicators.note: a speech is delivered when spoken, so we go by the sound of the words

blocks.note: something made to swing has been swayed

explanation.surface: A leather item set swinging as it is handed over.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede is leather with the flesh side rubbed to a soft napped finish, used for shoes and jackets.

clue.text: Peak, we hear, invariably referred to as high

definitions.text: Peak, we hear, invariably referred to as high

blocks.clueFragment: Peak, we hear, invariably referred to as high
blocks.note: surface reading: a mountain top that people always call high

blocks.clueFragment: Peak, we hear, invariably referred to as high
blocks.note: setter's reading: pique, resentment, sounds like peak, and this word for it only ever appears in the phrase 'in high' it

explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' turns peak into pique, offence taken; the answer is the word for that feeling which is almost always found after 'high'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dudgeon means a fit of indignant resentment, a sense of offence, and survives mainly in the set phrase high dudgeon.

clue.text: Contractor's footnote on tick

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another is added after it, so the first-named piece goes second

blocks.note: a tick and a trice are both an instant
PS, postscript, is a note added at the foot of a letter

explanation.surface: A builder's addendum attached to an item checked off on a list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contractor' suggests a builder; it is a muscle that contracts.
explanation.definitionFit: The triceps is the large muscle at the back of the upper arm, and muscles work by contracting.

clue.text: Prudish about the sexes meeting, or relaxed?

indicators.note: about means around, so this piece wraps the next

blocks.note: coy here means bashful or prim
M for male beside F for female

explanation.surface: Is a person squeamish about men and women mixing, or laid-back about it?
explanation.definitionFit: Comfy is an informal word for comfortable, at ease and physically relaxed.

clue.text: Could they be on the rocks with bad balances? Right!

definitions.text: Could they be on the rocks

indicators.note: something gone bad is spoiled, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A broke account holder is on the rocks with poor bank balances, and agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the rocks' suggests financial ruin; read literally, it is where these shellfish cling.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnacles are marine crustaceans that fix themselves to rocks, ship hulls and piers in the tidal zone.

clue.text: Horses in back-to-back races

indicators.note: placed back-to-back means set side by side, one directly after the other

blocks.note: blood means lineage or race, as in royal blood
stock also means lineage, as in of noble stock

explanation.surface: Racehorses running in two consecutive races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Races' looks like contests; here it means ancestries, and two words for that are joined.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloodstock is the collective term for thoroughbred horses bred for racing, valued for their pedigree.

clue.text: Wears t-this loosely? Exactly!

indicators.note: loosely suggests letters set free from their order and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the stammered word supplies an extra T

explanation.surface: Someone stammers that they wear this garment baggy, and the setter agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammer supplies the second T the letters need, and the whole clue describes the garment too.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweatshirt is a loose cotton jersey with long sleeves, normally worn casually and baggy.

clue.text: Furnishing periodical with set of figures

blocks.note: periodical in the sense of happening now and then
a table is an arranged set of figures

explanation.surface: A magazine with a page of statistics, as if describing a publication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Periodical' looks like a magazine; here it is an adjective, happening at intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: An occasional table is a small portable piece of furniture used as needed, so it counts as a furnishing.

clue.text: Game's up within seconds!

indicators.note: within means inside, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: sport's, game is, read as one word
taken as written

explanation.surface: An announcement that the match is over in moments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seconds' looks like time; it is the verb, as when someone seconds a motion.
explanation.definitionFit: To second a proposal is to back it formally, so seconds and supports are verb synonyms.

clue.text: Tie in cause of misery with money

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: the bane of one's life is its source of misery
to knot is to tie

explanation.surface: Money troubles bound up with whatever makes you wretched.
explanation.definitionFit: A banknote is paper currency issued by a bank, so it is a form of cash.

clue.text: Special sole pad to protect foot lever

indicators.note: special suggests a made-to-order version, so these letters are rearranged
to protect something is to surround it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
ft is the abbreviation for foot

explanation.surface: An orthopaedic insole cushion that guards the foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot' does double duty: it supplies FT and is part of the definition 'foot lever'.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft pedal is the left pedal of a piano, worked by the player's foot to quieten the tone.

clue.text: Let down, female starts to peak

indicators.note: starts says this piece comes at the beginning, ahead of the other

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
to let down is to lower

explanation.surface: Disappointed, a woman begins climbing to the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let down' looks like disappointed; it means lowered.
explanation.definitionFit: To flower is to reach the best stage of development, a verb sense like bloom or flourish.

clue.text: Girl models a little number in black

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the short form of number
jet black, the glossy black stone

explanation.surface: A girl shows off a small item, a little black dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little number' sounds like a dress; here it is just the abbreviation N.
explanation.definitionFit: Janet is a common given name for a woman, and crosswords use any such name to define the word girl.

clue.text: Jolly little woman on the bottle

blocks.note: Jo March, from Louisa May Alcott's Little Women
a vial is a small bottle

explanation.surface: A cheerful little lady who has taken to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second. Jo is the heroine of the novel Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: Jovial means cheerful and good-humoured, and jolly is an adjective synonym for that merry mood.

clue.text: Spare tyre will appear after this large meal!

definitions.text: Spare tyre will appear after this

blocks.clueFragment: Spare tyre will appear after this
blocks.note: first meaning: a burst tyre, after which the spare goes on
second meaning: a huge feast, informal

explanation.walkthrough: A spare tyre is also a roll of belly fat, which a big meal produces, so the first definition hints at both senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyre that bursts while driving is called this, and the same informal noun means a lavish, filling feast.

clue.text: Singer's perch

blocks.note: first meaning: a man with the lowest singing voice
second meaning: a spiny-finned fish related to the perch

explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer's perch' suggests a bird's roost; both nouns are separate definitions, with the 's meaning is.
explanation.definitionFit: A bass sings the lowest male vocal part, and the same spelling names an edible fish of the perch kind.

clue.text: Keep quiet about race position of an also-ran

indicators.note: about means around, so this piece wraps the other

blocks.note: sh is the call for quiet
a race is a sporting event

explanation.surface: Say nothing about where a losing runner finished.
explanation.definitionFit: An also-ran finishes outside the medals, and seventh place is one such lowly finishing slot.

clue.text: Quick bite from dog biscuit

blocks.note: first meaning: a sudden bite at something
second meaning: a crisp biscuit

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a dog snatching a biscuit; the two parts are separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogs snap when they bite suddenly, and a ginger snap is a thin brittle biscuit.

clue.text: Train, say, for this course

indicators.note: say asks us to go by how a word is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: a suite is the train of attendants following a dignitary

explanation.surface: Practise, for instance, for this part of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a verb; it is a retinue, which a suite also is.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the dessert course of a meal is commonly called the sweet.

clue.text: Rare catch made of unusual fish

indicators.note: something made is constructed, so these letters are reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An angler boasts of a rare catch of some exotic fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' is not marine: an odd fish is an eccentric person.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone an odd fish or a real character both mean an eccentric person with unusual ways.
